column1: # Per-file naming-exemption ledger for the directory-size and naming gate
# (issue #6054). scripts/lib/dirgate-grandfather.tsv pins the CAP check;
# this file separately pins the NAMING check, one row per already-violating
# file, deliberately kept apart from the cap ledger:
#   - a naming exemption is decided by a file's EXACT basename, never by a
#     directory's aggregate file count. Folding it into a comma-separated
#     cell on the cap ledger's one-row-per-directory shape made "the list
#     only shrinks" unenforceable by structure -- nothing stops someone
#     silently APPENDING a name inside a 27-name cell, and a new name
#     buried in one mutated mega-line is not visible in a diff the way a
#     new row is,
#   - two people fixing naming violations in different files of the same
#     directory in parallel PRs would conflict on that one shared line;
#     one row per file lets both prune their own row cleanly, and
#   - a directory can, in principle, need naming exemptions without ever
#     being a cap offender -- this file's rows are independent of whether
#     `dir` also has a row in dirgate-grandfather.tsv, EXCEPT that
#     tools/golangci-lint-dirgate/grandfather.go's generator currently
#     requires it (see that script): today every real exemption sits inside
#     an already cap-grandfathered directory, so a naming-exempt row for a
#     directory with no cap row is treated as a ledger error rather than
#     silently accepted.
# Columns (tab-separated): dir<TAB>file
#   dir  - package directory path relative to the go/ module root (same key
#          space as dirgate-grandfather.tsv).
#   file - the exact qualifying-file basename in `dir` that already
#          violated the sibling-subpackage naming rule when this row was
#          pinned (e.g. a name matching a subpackage directory, or that
#          name plus an underscore prefix -- see naming.go's
#          detectNamingViolations for the exact rule).
# A row exempts ONLY that exact file. A brand-new file that also collides
# with a subpackage name is NEVER covered by another file's row, even in
# the same directory -- it is reported immediately, regardless of the
# directory's cap state. This is the fix for the #6054 follow-up defect:
# the earlier design gated the whole directory's naming check on whether
# its aggregate count was at or below the cap ledger's pinned peak, which
# silently swallowed brand-new violations for as long as the epic's
# move-issues (#6056-#6062) kept shrinking that count -- exactly backwards.
# HARD FAIL, not a soft note: unlike a cap row that has shrunk below the
# cap (which scripts/verify-dirgate.sh --all only nudges toward removal),
# a naming-exempt row whose file has been moved, renamed, or removed --
# and so no longer exists, or no longer collides with its sibling
# subpackage -- makes `scripts/verify-dirgate.sh --all` FAIL outright. The
# PR that fixes the violation must delete this row in the same change;
# see dirgate_verify_naming_exempt_ledger in scripts/lib/dirgate-core.sh.
# The list only shrinks: remove a row once its file has actually moved
# into the sibling subpackage (or been renamed/removed so it no longer
# collides) -- never add a new row for a violation introduced after #6054
# landed; that violation must be fixed or given its own justified
# //nolint:dirgate marker instead.
# Seeded at #6054 landing (follow-up pass) from the pre-existing tree (see
# #6053), computed by walking every dirgate-grandfather.tsv directory's
# qualifying files against detectNamingViolations.
